answer_1.quote: The motivation behind the out-of-domain set is to facilitate the practical use of acceptability judgments for improving language generation.
answer_1.outputs: The paper uses machine translation and paraphrase generation models to produce out-of-domain sentences for the RuCoLA benchmark, which are then evaluated for acceptability.

answer_2.quote: We obtain the PenLP measure for each sentence by computing its log-probability (computed as a sum of token log-probabilities) from the ruGPT3-medium model.

answer_4.quote: We conduct a human evaluation on the entire in-domain test set and 50% of the out-of-domain test set. The pay rate is on average $6.3/hr, and the task design is similar to Stage 1 in §3.3 (see also Table , Appendix B.1) with a few exceptions.
answer_4.guideline: The annotators are given detailed instructions describing the task, explaining the labels, and showing plenty of examples. The instruction is available at any time during both the training and main annotation phases.
